title: Personnel of Sharkey's band at Nick's and the Saturday Night Swing Session
summary: Del Zane, Johnny Castang and others in the six-piece band, which repeated on CBS's swing session via Ted Husing.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Back to Sharky and Nick's, who else was in the band? Who was the piano player?

We had several, but the one who stayed along with us was a boy from Philadelphia, Del Zane, Z-A-N-E. It's new to me. Well he played on a radio station in Philadelphia for quite a while. What was the big station there? W-P-E-N is one. No, it is not the one, the other one. He was a staff pianist on that station for quite a while. Excellent piano player.
Did you have a bass player there?

W-P-E-N-E. We took Bradley and Johnny Castang came to New York. He played drums with us. When Henry Adler left, we used Johnny Castang. And of course he wasn't supposed to play because he just got to New York. He didn't have his union card, but we arranged it with the union and it was very nice to let Johnny come in on the job.
Did you have a guitar, a banjo?

W-P-E-N-E. No, no guitar. Three rhythm and three horns, six pieces. And we made that Saturday Night Swing Session, CBS had at the time. And I believe we broke the record by going back within a month. Nobody had ever repeated on the program. And Ted Husing was more or less our very godfather. He came in next and he liked the band so much that he arranged for us to go on that Saturday night swing session.
I'm wondering about that now. Sharpie had a guitar player named Bill Bourgeois or something.
No, no, it was me, Bill Bourgeois. But later we had Clayton Doerr, what he called Sunshine, played guitar. He had real thick glasses, close, near-sighted.
